confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors are based on web-search summaries of cost-of-living aggregators (traveltables.com, livingcost.org, citycost.org, mylifeelsewhere.com, whereandwhen.net, expatistan.com). They put an inexpensive meal at about USD 3.5-3.7, a mid-range meal for two at about USD 25-31, a cappuccino at about USD 2.6-2.9 and a 0.5 L domestic draught beer at about USD 1.6-2.05. I nudged these figures up a little for July 2026 and for restaurant serving prices. The cocktail estimate rests on weaker data: a crowd-sourced figure of about NT$200 (date unknown) and bar-guide ranges of NT$120-350, so I used a moderate bar price of about NT$250. The search found no reliable aggregated price for wine by the glass in Kaohsiung. The only Kaohsiung figure was NT$250 at one restaurant, and that may be a BYO-related fee rather than a glass price. Taipei glasses were reported at NT$300-500, so the wine anchor is a bounded estimate based on its usual local premium over beer and its parity with cocktails. Accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates for the July summer period, not checked against live listings, so they are less certain. The RBA rate is the 18 November 2026 4pm AEST observation as reported in search results that reference the RBA exchange-rates page.
comparable_city_reasoning: Kaohsiung is Taiwan's second-tier major city. Aggregators consistently show it as about 10-20% cheaper than Taipei and close to Taichung. Its prices are well below Japan and South Korea but above most Southeast Asian cities. Accommodation estimates assume rates somewhat below Taipei's, with typical Taiwanese hostel and budget-hotel pricing.
